examples.text: Der wollte mal erleben, wie es ist, richtig betrunken zu sein. Er hat sich die halbe Flasche reingezogen und war auch gut angeheitert.
examples.translation: He wanted to know what it's like being properly drunk. He downed half the bottle, and was pretty tipsy.

examples.text: Ich habe mir gestern gleich die ganze Staffel reingezogen.
examples.translation: I just watched the whole season yesterday.

glosses: (sich etwas reinziehen) auf irgendeine Weise sinnlich erfahren bzw. ausprobieren (z.B. schmecken, fühlen)
betrachten; angucken; anschauen

examples.text: Ich hab' mir gestern einen Film reingezogen.

anhören

examples.text: Hast du dir schon den neuen Song von XYZ reingezogen?

examples.text: Sollen wir uns noch 'nen Burger reinziehen?

glosses: To pull something, so that it comes inside.

examples.text: After falling out of the boat, the crew pulled him in.

glosses: To approach or drive up to a place and come to a stop; to park by driving frontways into a parking spot.

examples.text: A car just pulled in our driveway.

glosses: To approach a station; to arrive at a station.

examples.text: Quick! The train's pulling in.

The herd mentality appears strong at Cardiff. When the train pulls in, the majority of folk jam themselves into the car straight in front of them, while I walk to the back unit to share the rear car with just two other people.

glosses: To arrest someone; to take someone to a police station because they may have done something.

examples.text: She was pulled in for questioning.

glosses: To earn [money].

examples.text: He pulls in a lot of money.

glosses: To tighten a sail by pulling on a rope.

examples.text: pull in the main sheet

translations.source_sense_description: auf irgendeine Weise sinnlich erfahren bzw. ausprobieren

glosses: To record the departure or withdrawal of someone or something (such as guests, employees, books, etc.).

examples.text: He checked his favorite mystery out for the twenty-third time.
The desk clerk checked out the family that had been staying in room 322.

glosses: To record one's departure from a workplace, hotel, restaurant, etc.

examples.text: Be sure to check out of the hotel before noon.
I'm done shopping, so I'll go check out now.
[…] the singer person is checking out from the first floor suite next week, […]
"Relax," said the night man / "We are programmed to receive / You can check out any time you like / But you can never leave!"
At 9:30 am, 12 inmates were checked out to the dispensary.

glosses: To examine, inspect, look at closely, ogle; to investigate; to gather information so as to make a decision.

examples.text: He was hanging out at the beach, checking out the young women in bikinis.
He checked out the rumor, and managed to verify that it was true.
Check it out! Best prices in town.
Check this out! They just arrested the Mayor!

If Mr. Brill had been interested in accuracy, he might have read the written statement I presented that night. I was speaking on my own behalf because I felt that the Darts management deserved my support. Mr. Brill might even have asked me about my testimony. Instead he chose to check out his half-facts with others. His resultant report was inaccurate and divisive.

glosses: To obtain source code (and/or other material) from a source control repository so that one can modify it (and often later \"check in\" the modified version back).
To become uninterested in an activity and cease to participate in more than a perfunctory manner; to become uncooperative.

examples.text: The purpose of this exercise was to ignite reactions from students, but over the few years I used it, it backfired, culminating in a situation where I lost a significant number of the white students, who just "checked out" for the rest of the semester.

glosses: To become catatonic or otherwise nonresponsive.

examples.text: Even during those years, there would be a lot of times she just checked out. She would be sitting there looking at her nails and she'd just be gone.

glosses: To leave in a hurry.
To die.

examples.text:
Steve: (referring to his girlfriend attempting suicide in front of both of them) Look, I was just an observer.
Bishop: You haven't answered my question.
Steve: Well, what do you think?
Bishop: We'll never know, will we?
Steve: Well, say I just sat there—or we just sat there—and watched her check out. Think that would have been crazy?

With a bottle full of sleeping pills and a long list of sins
She'd already planned on checking out before she checked in

glosses: To prove (after an investigation) to be the case, or to be in order.

examples.text: The first two leads check out; I'll assume the third one is also valid.
Their stories checked out.
A comparison test was made with this weapon in laboratory. It definitely checks out as the murder gun.

MySQL checks the validity of the account name and password, and checks whether the connection is coming from a host that's allowed to connect [...]. If everything checks out, MySQL accepts the connection.

glosses: To visit the oche for the last time and clear one's remaining points to win the game.

translations.source_sense_description: auf irgendeine Weise sinnlich erfahren bzw. ausprobieren

glosses: Se cogner.

examples.text: Aïe ! Je me suis tapé contre le bord du placard.
Arrête de te taper la tête contre les murs ! Tu es fou ?

glosses: Faire, se farcir, se coltiner, se faire imposer (quelque chose, en particulier un travail peu ou pas du tout gratifiant).

examples.text: Caroline se lassa vite du rôle de femme de politicien, et elle commença à se faire appeler C.C. pour montrer son indépendance. Quand Lucius était vice-gouverneur, elle devait se taper toutes les obligations qui barbaient les épouses de gouverneurs : les clubs de macramé, les centenaires, les mimes à la foire du comté, les élèves des écoles qui chantaient des cantiques dans les centres commerciaux.
Faut que tu te lèves, que tu te tapes le R.E.R., que tu répondes pas quand le patron te donne des ordres pour taffer un truc de merde. Trop relou.
Quand on voit le résultat, on n’a pas envie de se taper des générations de mous de la cuisse au teint verdâtre de poireau bouilli !

glosses: Recevoir ou être victime de quelque chose d’indésirable.

examples.text: On s’est tapé trois heures de discussions qui n’ont abouti à rien.
Il s’est tapé la honte devant tout le monde.

glosses: Avoir une relation sexuelle avec (quelqu’un).

examples.text: Je me rappelle m’être tapé des filles dans les buffalos, les remorques de tramways, qu’on dételait après les heures de grand trafic et qu’on garait en différents points de la périphérie.
Alors le soir, quand ils rentrent à l'Ibis, deux, trois Ricard plus tard, ils se tapent leur assistante ou une occasionnelle. C'est glauque, c'est vrai.
Il était avec un cageot je ne te raconte pas. Une nana immonde. Même coincé sur une île déserte avec un thon pareil, je préférerais me taper une chèvre!
Ce qui me rend malade ce n'est pas que tu puisses te taper cette guenon, mais qu'un looser de ton espèce puisse ainsi me prendre pour une conne en draguant sans retenue n'importe quoi.
Hahahi ! Tu penses que je veux me taper Édith, t'es encore plus largué que je pensais, toé !

translations.source_sense_description: auf irgendeine Weise sinnlich erfahren bzw. ausprobieren

glosses: Forme pronominale de faire.

examples.text: Mais comment s’est fait ce choix, et quelles conséquences cela aura-t-il sur les automobilistes, on vous explique.
Au sein de la majorité, les choses se sont faites naturellement.

glosses: Suivi d’un verbe transitif à l’infinitif, sert à construire des tournures équivalentes à la voix passive, où le sujet grammatical subit l’action.

examples.text: Il s’est fait mordre ≈ Il a été mordu.
Mon œil s’est fait peintre et a fait resplendir la forme de ta beauté sur le tableau de mon cœur ; ma personne est le cadre qui l’enferme ; et c’est un chef-d’œuvre de perspective :
